steps.title: The Dundee Hills
steps.body: The Dundee Hills AVA, created in 2005, is the Willamette Valley's historic heart, where David Lett and others first planted. The hills rise to about 300 m, facing south and east, above the valley's fog and frost. Famous producers include Eyrie, Domaine Drouhin Oregon, Domaine Serene and Archery Summit.

steps.title: Jory soil
steps.body: The Dundee Hills' soil is Jory, a deep, red, iron-rich clay loam formed from ancient volcanic basalt. It drains well and holds moderate water. Its Pinot Noir is known for red fruit, elegance and silky texture. Other AVAs have different soils: marine sediments in Yamhill-Carlton give darker fruit, and loess in Chehalem Mountains.

options: A red, iron-rich clay from volcanic basalt
steps.explanation: It gives the Dundee Hills' elegant Pinot.

steps.title: Other AVAs
steps.body: The Willamette Valley has 11 nested AVAs, including Eola-Amity Hills, cooled by the Van Duzer winds, Yamhill-Carlton, Ribbon Ridge, McMinnville, Chehalem Mountains and Laurelwood District. Each has distinct soils, volcanic, marine sediment or loess, giving different Pinot styles.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Dundee Hills are the historic heart
Jory, red volcanic clay, gives elegant Pinot
Eleven AVAs show different soils and styles
